chunks: I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: “What do you think about what these people take from this khums from the land of jizyah, and they take from the dahāqīn the jizyah of their heads? Is there upon them, in that, any fixed obligation?”

So he said: “What was binding upon them was what they themselves accepted upon themselves, and the Imam has no more than the jizyah. If the Imam wishes, he places that upon their heads, and there is nothing upon their wealth; and if he wishes, then it is upon their wealth, and there is nothing upon their heads.”
So I said: “Then this khums?” He said: “This is only something concerning which the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله made an agreement with them.”

key_terms.أَمْوَالِهِمْ: their wealth or property, meaning financial assets subject to levy
key_terms.الدَّهَاقِينِ: landowners or local notables from whom jizyah is being taken
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam, the lawful authority who determines the mode of assessment
key_terms.الْجِزْيَةِ: jizyah, the tax due from non-Muslim subjects under agreed terms
key_terms.الْخُمُسِ: khums, a one-fifth levy mentioned here in relation to lands under treaty arrangement
key_terms.رُءُوسِهِمْ: their persons or heads, meaning per-capita liability
key_terms.صَالَحَهُمْ: made a treaty or settlement with them
key_terms.مُوَظَّفٌ: fixed or prescribed as an assigned obligation

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about jizyah, khums, and the authority of the Imam in taxation?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the liability of jizyah rests on the terms accepted by those subject to it, and that the Imam does not take beyond the jizyah itself. It also distinguishes between levying it on persons or on wealth, and clarifies that the mentioned khums was based on a settlement made by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله with them.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: I asked Abu Abdullah (Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq), peace be upon him: "What about what these people collect as khums from the lands of jizya and what they take from the dahahin (landowners) as the poll tax (jizya) on their persons? Is there a fixed obligation upon them in this regard?"

Imam (as) replied: "They are bound by what they agreed upon for themselves. The Imam is entitled to no more than the jizya. If the Imam wishes, he may impose it on their persons, leaving their wealth untouched. Alternatively, if he wishes, he may impose it on their wealth, exempting their persons.
As for this khums, it is only something that the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, made a treaty with them concerning."
